name: Grayson Highlands
unique: Open highland balds at 5,000 feet with wild ponies grazing among granite outcrops, and the Appalachian Trail crossing Mount Rogers, Virginia's highest point.
buzz: The ponies are habituated and will investigate your lunch; the Wilburn Ridge loop is the classic. Weather changes fast and the wind is constant.

name: Arlington National Cemetery
unique: The national cemetery on the Potomac, with the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, the changing of the guard, Kennedy's grave and rows of markers on the hills.
buzz: Sobering and beautifully kept. Take the tram if you want to cover the ground, and stay for the guard change.

name: Shenandoah National Park and Skyline Drive
dates: Year round, Skyline Drive sections close for ice
unique: 105 miles of ridge road along the crest of the Blue Ridge with 75 overlooks, and 500 miles of trail through oak and hemlock forest including Hawksbill, the park's highest summit, reached from a trailhead in Page County.
buzz: The drive is the attraction and the traffic knows it. Regulars go before eight in the morning, park at Thornton Gap and walk up Stony Man instead of driving the whole road.

name: Floyd Country Store Friday Night
unique: A 1910 general store with a potbelly stove where a live old time band plays and anyone can join the flatfooting and two-step on the worn wooden floor.
buzz: Locals and visitors agree it is the most welcoming room in Appalachia; get there early for a seat and expect to be pulled into a dance.

name: Monticello
unique: Jefferson's mountaintop house with its dumbwaiters, alcove beds and clock-driven calendar, plus the reconstructed slave quarters that complicate the postcard.
buzz: The slavery exhibits get strong praise for honesty; the house tour is timed and the grounds need another hour. Book the first slot.

name: Mount Vernon
unique: George Washington's plantation on the Potomac, with the mansion, the tomb, the slave quarters, a working farm and a distillery.
buzz: The house tour and the slave memorial together tell the whole story, and the river view is beautiful. Allow three hours.

name: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with Art Nouveau, African art, Faberge and a sculpture garden, plus a strong photography program.
buzz: Free and world class, with a good cafe and a sculpture garden. The Faberge collection is the surprise.

name: Busch Gardens Williamsburg
dates: March–early January, Christmas Town in winter
unique: A theme park built as a set of European hamlets in a wooded ravine, with eight coasters including a launched wing coaster and a wooden coaster that regularly ranks among the best in the world, plus a show schedule and a beer hall.
buzz: Coaster people come for the lineup and stay for the landscaping, which is the thing everyone mentions. Summer crowds and parking prices are the complaints.

name: Luray Caverns and the Great Stalacpipe Organ
unique: A vast limestone cavern where a lithophone built into the stalactites plays music through the rock itself, the world's largest musical instrument, and it actually works.
buzz: Visitors are surprised by how good the organ recital is; the cavern is commercial but genuinely spectacular. The garden maze next door is a decent add on.

name: Marine Corps War Memorial
unique: The Iwo Jima flag raising statue in bronze, with a view across the river to the Washington monuments and a nightly sunset ceremony in summer.
buzz: The scale of the statue surprises people, and the skyline view is excellent. Free and quick.

name: Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts
unique: The only national park for the performing arts, with a covered amphitheater and lawn seating under the trees, plus a barn theater for smaller shows.
buzz: Bring a picnic and a blanket for the lawn. The sound is good and the setting is hard to beat.

name: Chrysler Museum of Art
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with a strong European and American collection, an entire wing of glass from ancient to studio, and a working glass studio where you can watch a piece being blown or book a session to make one.
buzz: Free admission for a collection this size is the thing visitors cannot get over. The glass studio demonstrations and the Tiffany window are the usual favorites.

name: Devil's Bathtub
unique: A series of natural plunge pools carved into sandstone at the end of a creek-wading and boulder-hopping route through Jefferson National Forest.
buzz: People love it and warn the route is unmarked, slippery and not for flip-flops. Go early; it is a locals' secret that leaked.

name: Historic Jamestowne
company: National Park Service and Preservation Virginia
unique: The actual site of the 1607 fort, where archaeologists are still digging and have found the bones and artifacts of the first English settlement, with a memorial church, a museum of the findings and a walk along the James where the first ships tied up.
buzz: Seeing the excavation in progress is what separates it from the recreated settlement next door. Rangers and archaeologists explain the ongoing work, and the church tower is the oldest standing structure on the site.

name: Old Fiddler's Convention
unique: The oldest and largest old time and bluegrass convention in the world, six days of competitions in forty categories at Felts Park, with hundreds of musicians jamming under tarps and campers in the field until three in the morning.
buzz: Musicians describe it as the center of the old time universe and non musicians are surprised they can walk in and listen to world class picking for the price of a day ticket. Camping fills a year ahead.

name: American Shakespeare Center
unique: A recreation of Shakespeare's indoor Blackfriars theater, lit by chandeliers with the house lights on, where actors can see and talk to the audience.
buzz: The staging is energetic and the tickets are cheap for the quality; the town of Staunton is a good base.

name: Battleship Wisconsin
unique: An Iowa class battleship docked at Nauticus, with turrets, crew quarters and a deck you can walk, plus a science center next door.
buzz: The ship is enormous and the tour is self guided, so you can go at your pace. Good for kids.

name: Chincoteague Pony Swim
unique: Saltwater cowboys herd wild ponies across the channel at slack tide, then auction the foals to keep the herd small, a 100-year old ritual on a barrier island.
buzz: It is genuinely crowded and hot, and people still call it unforgettable. Watch from the water or a boat, not the packed shore.

name: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
unique: The mountain pass that opened the westward trail through the Appalachians, with earthworks, a visitor center and a ridge trail across three states.
buzz: The view from the pinnacle is worth the climb, and the history is foundational. Free.

name: Frontier Culture Museum
dates: Year round, costumed interpreters most days
unique: Four working farm sites rebuilt from 17th and 18th century England, Ireland, Germany and West Africa, plus an American farmstead, spread across a valley field and staffed by interpreters who explain how each place fed the migration that filled the Shenandoah.
buzz: The West African farm and the German farm are the parts people did not expect, and the interpreters stay in role without lecturing. Plan three hours and wear walking shoes, the site is a long loop.

name: Jamestown Settlement
unique: A living history museum with replicas of the Susan Constant, a Powhatan village and a fort, telling the 1607 story.
buzz: Kids can climb the ships and try on armor, and the museum covers the hard history of the colony. Good for a family day.

name: Lewis Ginter Botanical Garden
unique: Fifty acres of themed gardens with a conservatory, a children's garden, a rose garden and a lake, plus a holiday lights show.
buzz: The conservatory is the winter win and the children's garden is genuinely good. Holiday lights sell out.

name: Maymont
unique: A 100-acre Gilded Age estate with a Romanesque mansion, Japanese and Italian gardens, and a Virginia wildlife exhibit with otters, bobcats and black bears.
buzz: Free grounds and a small mansion fee; the gardens are gorgeous in spring and the wildlife exhibits are better than expected for kids.

name: Museum of the Shenandoah Valley
customer: Art and garden people, regional history students
unique: A regional museum with six galleries of valley furniture, silver and folk art, a 1794 house built by the founder of Winchester, and six acres of formal gardens and trails on the same hill.
buzz: The gardens and the Glen Burnie house get as much praise as the exhibits, and the miniature house collection is the thing kids remember. Closed Mondays, which catches people out.

name: Natural Tunnel State Park
unique: A 850 foot natural tunnel carved by a creek through a mountain, with a chairlift, a train line through it and trails above.
buzz: The tunnel is genuinely dramatic and the chairlift saves the climb. Go when the train passes through.

name: University of Virginia Rotunda
unique: Jefferson's rotunda and the lawn of pavilions and student rooms, a UNESCO World Heritage site and a working university.
buzz: The lawn is the walk and the rotunda tour explains Jefferson's design. Free and central.

name: Yorktown Battlefield
unique: The battlefield where Cornwallis surrendered in 1781, with earthworks, a siege line and a driving tour through the woods.
buzz: The ranger talks make the siege make sense, and the earthworks are well preserved. Pair it with the American Revolution Museum.

name: American Revolution Museum at Yorktown
unique: A museum of the whole Revolution told from the bottom up, with a gallery of period weapons and documents, an outdoor Continental Army encampment and a farm where interpreters fire muskets and cook over open fires, on the ground where the war ended.
buzz: The encampment artillery demonstrations are what people remember, and the exhibits on enslaved and Native people are treated seriously. It is a state museum that behaves like a national one.

name: Colonial Williamsburg
unique: Eighty-eight original and reconstructed buildings on the actual 18th century capital, with tradespeople who blacksmith, bind books and argue politics in character.
buzz: The ticket price draws complaints, but the trades and the evening programs are rated excellent. Go in spring or fall; summer heat is brutal in wool.

name: Grand Caverns
dates: Year round, spelunking trips by reservation
unique: The oldest continually operating show cave in the country, opened for tours in 1806, with shield formations found almost nowhere else and hundreds of signatures from Civil War soldiers on the walls, including a battalion roster written in candle smoke.
buzz: Guides point out the 1863 signatures and the shield formations, and the cave runs a wild caving trip for people who want to crawl instead of walk. Reviews single out the guides.

name: Barter Theatre
unique: The state theater of Virginia, founded during the Depression when actors accepted produce as admission, still producing a full season in a 1930s playhouse.
buzz: Production values are high for a small town and the history is charming; dinner on Main Street is part of the night.

name: Big Schloss Trail
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A four mile round trip from the Wolf Gap saddle to a rock outcrop on the Virginia and West Virginia line, named by German settlers for a castle, with a hundred mile view and a short exposed scramble that feels bigger than the map suggests.
buzz: One of the most photographed views in the northern Valley and the reason Wolf Gap campground fills on fall weekends. The last quarter mile is a rock hop, not a trail.

name: Breaks Interstate Park
unique: The deepest gorge east of the Mississippi, a sixteen hundred foot cut in the Cumberland plateau that straddles the Virginia and Kentucky line, with overlooks on both rims, a lake, and whitewater releases on the Russell Fork in fall.
buzz: The Grand Canyon of the South nickname undersells the fall rafting, which runs Class IV and V releases a few weekends a year and sells out. The overlooks are a short walk from the parking lots.

name: Carter Mountain Orchard
unique: A pick your own orchard on a ridge above Charlottesville, with apple cider doughnuts, a bakery and a view of Monticello and the Blue Ridge.
buzz: The view and the doughnuts are the reason, and picking is a fall ritual. Go early on weekends.

name: Great Falls Park
unique: The Potomac compresses into a quarter mile of Class V rapids twenty minutes from the capital, with cliff-top overlooks and a boulder-strewn gorge.
buzz: Locals call it the best quick nature fix near DC; the River Trail scramble is the fun part. Parking fills by 10am on weekends.

name: Red Wing Roots Music Festival
unique: A three day roots and Americana festival in the meadow under the Natural Chimneys towers, with a bike valet, a creek for kids, camping on site and a lineup that mixes touring acts with valley bands.
buzz: People describe it as the festival that feels like a family reunion, small enough to see everything and with a reputation for treating the grounds well. Sells out most years.

name: Virginia Creeper Trail
company: Town of Damascus and the U.S. Forest Service
unique: A rail trail on the old Abingdon branch line, mostly downhill, crossing thirty trestles and running along Whitetop Laurel Creek through a gorge, with shuttle outfits in Damascus hauling riders and bikes to the top.
buzz: The sixteen mile Abingdon to Damascus stretch is open and the seventeen mile Damascus to Whitetop section is closed for Hurricane Helene repairs until April 2027. Rentals and shuttles are running for the open section.

name: Virginia Safari Park
unique: A 180 acre drive through safari where bison, zebra and elk stick their heads in your car, plus a walk through village with giraffes and kangaroos.
buzz: Buy the feed and accept that your car will be licked; the drive through is the fun and the walk through is a bonus. Go early.

name: White Rocks and Sand Cave via the Ewing Trail
unique: An eight mile climb from a valley trailhead to a sandstone cliff line on the Kentucky border, with Sand Cave, an overhang big enough to hold a house and a floor of loose sand, and a ridge walk to White Rocks with a view across three states.
buzz: The cave is the payoff and the climb is the price. Hikers warn that the last pitch is steep and that the sand floor is cold even in summer, and everyone says start early.

name: Birthplace of Country Music Museum
unique: A Smithsonian affiliate museum built on the story of the 1927 Bristol Sessions, when a talent scout recorded Jimmie Rodgers and the Carter Family in a hat factory and made the records that became country music, with listening stations for every session track.
buzz: The listening booths and the radio station inside are the highlight, and the museum makes the case for Bristol over Nashville without sneering. Musicians leave with a list of records to find.

name: Mabry Mill
unique: A water powered gristmill, sawmill and blacksmith shop on the Blue Ridge Parkway, with a millpond that reflects the whole thing and a weekend craft demonstration.
buzz: The most photographed spot on the Parkway and it earns it at dawn; the restaurant's buckwheat pancakes are a tradition.

name: Shenandoah Caverns
dates: Year round, American Celebration closes in winter
unique: The only Virginia cavern with an elevator down, and the one with bacon, strips of translucent flowstone that hang in sheets, plus a second building full of retired Rose Parade and presidential inauguration floats.
buzz: Guides point out the bacon formation first because that is what everyone photographs. The float warehouse next door surprises people more than the cave does.

name: Blue Ridge Tunnel
dates: Year round, daylight, bring a light
company: Nelson County and the City of Waynesboro
unique: A 4,273 foot railroad tunnel blasted through the Blue Ridge by hand between 1850 and 1858, abandoned for decades and reopened in 2020 as a flat gravel walk that goes from daylight into total darkness and back out the other side of the mountain.
buzz: People walk it with headlamps and describe the temperature drop and the water dripping from the ceiling. The climb back up from the west portal is the part that surprises everyone.

name: Burke's Garden
dates: Year round, best June and October
unique: An eight mile wide bowl in the top of a mountain, farmed since the 1740s by families who still work the bottom land, seen whole from the rim road where the valley floor lies a thousand feet below and the fields run to the base of the encircling ridge.
buzz: Called God's Thumbprint by locals and photographed from the overlook on Route 623. Drivers are asked to stay on the road and respect that every acre is somebody's farm.

name: First Landing State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: Twenty miles of trails through bald cypress swamp and maritime forest, a beach on the bay, and campground cabins built by the CCC in the 1930s, on the shore where the Jamestown colonists first came ashore.
buzz: The cypress swamp trail is unlike anything else in the state and the bay beach is calm enough for small children. Summer parking fills early.

name: Hungry Mother State Park
dates: Year round, beach Memorial Day–Labor Day
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: One of the six original Virginia state parks, built by the CCC around a mountain lake with a sand beach, a restaurant on the water, cabins and trails that climb to a rock overlook of the whole valley.
buzz: The lake beach and the restaurant are why families return, and the cabin reservations open a year out and go fast. The name comes from a legend about a woman and her child that the park does not oversell.

name: Leesburg Historic District
unique: A courthouse square of 18th and 19th century buildings, brick sidewalks, a brewery and restaurants, in the middle of Virginia wine country.
buzz: The downtown is walkable and busy on weekends, with good lunch spots and a farmers market.

name: Lexington Historic District
unique: A small Shenandoah Valley town with Washington and Lee and VMI, Stonewall Jackson's house, a historic courthouse and brick streets.
buzz: The colleges and the old houses make a compact walk, and the VMI museum is free.

name: Mill Mountain Star
unique: A 88 foot neon star on a mountain above Roanoke, with a viewpoint over the valley and the city lights at night.
buzz: The drive up is easy and the view is the payoff, especially at dusk. Free.

name: Roanoke Pinball Museum
unique: Sixty machines from the 1950s onward, all playable, in a downtown space where the volunteer mechanics will explain how a flipper works.
buzz: Everything is on free play and the collection is well maintained; a cheap hour of joy in a city that needed one.

name: Shenandoah Apple Blossom Festival
dates: Late April into early May, ten days
customer: Families, parade crowds, marching band alumni
unique: Ten days of parades, a firefighter's rodeo, a carnival and a celebrity grand marshal in a city that closes its downtown for the blossom parade, running since 1924 and drawing over a hundred thousand people.
buzz: The Firefighters' Parade and the Pink and Green Show sell out, and locals either love the crowds or leave town. Hotels book a year ahead.

name: Virginia Aquarium and Marine Science Center
customer: Families, marine biology students, rainy day crowds
unique: A aquarium with a walk through tunnel under a 300,000 gallon tank, a river otter habitat and a stranding response team that rescues whales and sea turtles on the Virginia coast, with the rescue work explained rather than hidden.
buzz: The otters and the tunnel are the kid favorites and the staff talks about rehabilitation cases by name. Tickets are expensive enough that people look for the combination deals.

name: Virginia Beach Boardwalk
unique: A three mile oceanfront boardwalk with restaurants, a fishing pier, a statue of Neptune and separate bike and walking lanes.
buzz: The boardwalk is wide and clean, and the Neptune statue is the photo. Busy in summer, pleasant in the off season.

name: Agecroft Hall
unique: A Tudor manor house built in England in the 1500s, dismantled, shipped across the Atlantic and rebuilt on the James River in 1925, with the original glass and oak.
buzz: The story of the move is as interesting as the house; the gardens are quiet and the tours are personal.

name: Cape Henry Lighthouse
unique: The first lighthouse authorized by the federal government, finished in 1792 and still standing on the beach where the first English settlers landed, with a spiral stair you climb to a gallery looking straight down the Atlantic and into Chesapeake Bay.
buzz: The climb is 191 steps and the view from the top is the reason. The older tower leans slightly, which people notice on the way up.

name: Henderson Guitar Shop
cost: Free to visit, guitars by waitlist
unique: The workshop of a luthier who has built guitars for Eric Clapton and Doc Watson out of a shed in a Grayson County hollow, where he will show you the spruce tops he taps for tone and the neck blanks drying above the stove.
buzz: Visitors describe being handed a guitar to play and staying two hours. He is a legendary picker as well as a builder, and the wait for one of his instruments is measured in years.

name: New River Trail State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: Fifty seven miles of crushed gravel on an abandoned railroad grade along the New River, one of the oldest rivers in North America, with tunnels, trestles, a shot tower and river access points spread across four counties.
buzz: Riders do the whole length in a day and families do the Galax end. The surface is smooth enough for hybrids and the tunnels are cool in summer.

name: Shenandoah River Outfitters
unique: Canoe, kayak, raft and tube trips on the South Fork from a riverside base with cabins and tent sites, including a flatwater stretch that beginners can handle and a seven mile run past the Massanutten ridge.
buzz: The outfit runs shuttles all day and the staff put nervous beginners in the right boat. Tubing is slow and social in July when the river drops.

name: Virginia Elk Viewing Tours
dates: September and October, booked in advance
unique: Guided bus tours into the elk restoration zone in Buchanan County, run by state wildlife biologists during the fall rut, when bulls bugle across the reclaimed mine grasslands and the herd that was reintroduced in 2012 is now large enough to see in a morning.
buzz: Tours sell out quickly and people report dozens of animals on a good morning. The guides explain the reintroduction and the arguments around it rather than just pointing.

name: Virginia Museum of the Civil War at New Market
unique: The battlefield where 257 VMI cadets marched into the line in the rain in 1864 and broke it, now a museum with the flag they carried, a restored Bushong farm the fighting went through, and a walking trail over the same ground.
buzz: The cadet charge is the story everyone comes for and the museum tells it with the actual uniforms and a sound and light show. Reenactments in May draw crowds.

name: Wilderness Road State Park
dates: Park year round, fort weekends May–October
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A reconstructed 1775 frontier fort called Martin's Station on the road Daniel Boone widened into the Wilderness Road, staffed by interpreters in period clothing who demonstrate blacksmithing, militia drill and open hearth cooking at the edge of the Cumberland Gap.
buzz: The fort weekends are the reason to time a visit, and the interpreters stay in character without being precious about it. The park also has a trail along the old road bed.

name: Back of the Dragon
unique: Thirty two miles of Virginia Route 16 between Marion and Tazewell with more than three hundred curves, climbing over three mountains and dropping into the Clinch valley, promoted by the county as a riding road with a welcome center at each end.
buzz: Riders come from several states and rate it as technical rather than fast, with blind switchbacks and gravel in the turns. Weekdays are quiet and weekends bring groups.

name: Cedar Creek Battlefield
customer: Civil War students, driving tour people
unique: The ground of the October 1864 battle that decided control of the valley, with a self guided driving tour past the Heater farm, the 8th Vermont monument and the ridge where the Union line broke, plus ranger talks from the Belle Grove side.
buzz: The tour is well marked and free, and the story of the surprise attack at dawn is what guides spend their time on. Some visitors want more interpretive signage than exists.

name: Chateau Morrisette
unique: A winery on the Blue Ridge Parkway with a tasting room, a restaurant and a lawn, making wine since the 1970s.
buzz: The setting is the sell and the restaurant is good for lunch. Check hours in winter.

name: High Knob Tower
dates: Forest road open April–November, gate closed in winter
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
customer: View chasers, hang glider pilots, photographers
unique: A forest observation tower at 4,223 feet on the high point of the Cumberland plateau, with a platform that shows five states on a clear day and a launch ramp used by hang glider pilots who ride the ridge lift.
buzz: The drive up is steep and the gate closes in winter, which people learn the hard way. On a clear morning the view is the best in southwest Virginia.

name: Morven Park
unique: A 1,000 acre estate with a Greek Revival mansion, formal gardens, a carriage museum and equestrian grounds.
buzz: The carriage collection is the surprise, and the grounds are quiet. Check tour times.

name: Natural Bridge
unique: A 215-foot limestone arch that Jefferson called a wonder of the world, with a lost river, a saltpeter cave and a nightly illumination show.
buzz: People stop for an hour and stay for three; the evening light show is kitsch but charming. The walk is paved and easy.

name: Norfolk Botanical Garden
unique: Virginia's largest botanical garden, with more than sixty themed gardens, a tram ride through the whole property, a butterfly house in season and a bog full of carnivorous plants, on land first planted by Works Progress Administration crews in the 1930s.
buzz: The tram is worth the ticket for anyone with limited walking and the rose garden in May is the local photo spot. The butterfly house is the kid draw.

name: Seven Bends State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
customer: Paddlers, anglers, families with small kids
unique: A young state park on a seven mile serpentine stretch of the North Fork, with river access, a wade and swim beach, and bluff trails above the bends that look down on water looping back on itself.
buzz: The river access is the draw for canoeists and smallmouth anglers. Trails are easy and short, which makes it the park people bring grandparents and toddlers to.

name: Shenandoah River State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: Over five miles of river frontage on the South Fork with a canoe launch, a sandy beach, riverfront cabins and a bluff trail that looks down on the water, in the county that calls itself the canoe capital of Virginia.
buzz: The cabins book months out and the river access is the reason. Trails are well built and the park is quiet compared with the national park next door.

name: Shenandoah Valley Music Festival
dates: Mid July through Labor Day weekend, weekends
customer: Couples, symphony goers, bluegrass and Americana fans
unique: Concerts on the lawn and under the pavilion at Shrine Mont, an 1870s resort of white frame hotels and cottages in a mountain hollow, with a season that mixes symphony nights, bluegrass and tribute acts in a venue that holds a few hundred people.
buzz: People bring chairs, wine and dinner and sit on the slope. The setting is the review, over and over, along with how easy it is to get close to the stage.

name: Skyline Caverns
customer: Families, geology curious, DC day trippers
unique: One of the few caves in the world with anthodites, white spiked crystals that grow outward in every direction and are so fragile the tour stays behind glass, discovered by a state geologist in 1937 and opened the same year.
buzz: Guides explain why the anthodites cannot be touched and why they only form in a handful of caves. Smaller than Luray and less crowded, which people mention as the trade.

name: Taubman Museum of Art
unique: A free museum in a striking modern building with regional art, American painting, folk art and a sculpture gallery.
buzz: The building is the photo and the collection is free. Good rainy day stop.

name: Virginia Scenic Railway
dates: Selected days year round, fall color and holiday runs sell out
unique: Excursions from the 1902 Staunton depot, east through the Blue Ridge Tunnel on the active Norfolk Southern line or west along the Cowpasture River, with onboard dining in a restored car and a route no highway can match.
buzz: The eastbound run through the tunnel is the one people book first. Reviews praise the crew and the view from the dome seats and warn that the trip is about the ride, not the destination.

name: Water Country USA
unique: Virginia's largest water park, with a wave pool, a lazy river and a set of slides that includes a four person raft run and a bowl ride, in a park small enough to cover in a day without a plan.
buzz: People rate it as the best water park within a few hours of Richmond and warn about chair claims and locker lines. Go on a weekday in June.

name: Back Bay National Wildlife Refuge
dates: Daily, daylight, some areas closed in winter for waterfowl
unique: Nine thousand acres of marsh, dunes and barrier beach at the southern end of Virginia Beach, where the road ends and the wild beach begins, with a paddle trail through the back bay and a winter population of snow geese and tundra swans.
buzz: Birders come for the migration and paddlers for the quiet water. The walk down the beach to False Cape is a full day and there is no shade.

name: Belle Grove Plantation
company: Belle Grove Inc., National Trust for Historic Preservation
customer: Architecture people, enslaved history students, families
unique: A 1797 limestone manor house with a two story portico built by a German immigrant family, later the home of a slaveholding dynasty, with tours that cover the enslaved workers who built and ran it and the 1864 battle that swept across its fields.
buzz: The interpretation of slavery is the part visitors say changed their understanding, and the house itself is unrestored enough to feel real. Grounds are free to walk.

name: Massanutten Resort
customer: Families, skiers from DC, mountain bikers, golfers
unique: A 6,000 acre four season mountain with southern Virginia's largest ski hill, an indoor and outdoor waterpark, a lift served bike park and a summer adventure course, all on one ridge above the valley.
buzz: The waterpark is what sells it to families, the ski hill is small but close, and the bike trails have a serious following. Reviews warn about condo quality varying by unit.

name: Natural Chimneys Park
unique: Seven limestone towers up to 120 feet high left standing where a cave roof collapsed, in a county park with a campground, a pool and a creek, on the site of a resort that has drawn valley visitors since the 1800s.
buzz: Small enough to walk in ten minutes and strange enough to keep people an hour. The festival grounds beside the towers host the county's biggest music weekend each June.

name: Bryce Resort
dates: Year round, ski December–March, bike park April–November
customer: Beginner skiers, mountain bikers, families from DC
unique: A small four season mountain two hours from Washington with the state's most forgiving beginner slopes, a lift served bike park with jump lines, and a summer tubing hill, all in a valley with no other ski area within a hundred miles.
buzz: People describe it as where you learn to ski without paying resort prices, and the bike park has become the reason younger visitors come in summer. Lines are short, terrain is modest.

name: Downriver Canoe Company
customer: Families, first time paddlers, group trips
unique: Canoe, kayak and raft trips on the South Fork from a riverside base in Bentonville, running the stretch below the Front Royal bridges where the river braids into islands and the current does most of the work.
buzz: Shuttle drivers get people on the water fast and the staff talk beginners through the first riffle. Tubing in July is slow and social.

name: Elk Garden Trail
dates: Year round, road may close in winter
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
customer: Hikers, Appalachian Trail section hikers, photographers
unique: A high saddle at 4,200 feet where the Appalachian Trail crosses from Russell County into the Mount Rogers high country, with open balds, a spruce forest and a day use area that puts wild ponies and the state's highest ground within a few miles.
buzz: Section hikers use it as a start or finish and day hikers use it for the balds. The gravel road up is the usual complaint.

name: Norfolk Tides at Harbor Park
unique: Triple A baseball on the Elizabeth River with the downtown skyline behind the outfield, cheap tickets, a crab cake stand and a promenade where you can watch the game standing at a rail with a boat going by.
buzz: The ballpark is the reason people go even when the team is bad. Tickets are cheap, the food is local and the waterfront seats are the ones to ask for.

name: Ralph Stanley Museum
company: Ralph Stanley Museum and Traditional Mountain Music Center
customer: Bluegrass fans, musicians, Appalachian history people
unique: A museum to the Clinch Mountain Boys founder and his brother Carter, in a century old house on Clintwood's main street, with Stanley's instruments, stage clothes, recordings and a listening room where the mountaintop removal of the old time sound is explained track by track.
buzz: Fans make pilgrimages and leave saying the listening stations are the best part. The staff will talk about the Bristol sessions and the Stanley family for as long as you let them.

name: Southern Gap Outdoor Adventure
customer: ATV riders, elk watchers, camping families
unique: A county built trailhead on a reclaimed mine site at the base of the Spearhead Trails network, with cabins and RV sites, ATV and side by side rentals, and guided elk tours into the herd that was reintroduced to these mountains after a century and a half.
buzz: Riders come for the hundred miles of trail and stay two days. The elk tours are the surprise, and sightings are common at dawn on the grassland the mine left behind.

name: Trail of the Lonesome Pine Outdoor Drama
customer: Theatre people, families, Appalachian history fans
unique: The official outdoor drama of Virginia, staged since 1963 in an amphitheater cut into the mountain above Big Stone Gap, telling the story of the feuding families and the coal boom that turned a valley town into a company town.
buzz: Volunteers build the sets and the cast comes back year after year. Locals bring blankets and picnic before the show, and the mountain backdrop does half the work.

name: Wayne C. Henderson Music Festival and Guitar Competition
customer: Bluegrass and old time fans, pickers, families
unique: A one day festival in the picnic area at Grayson Highlands where the guitar competition is the main event, with contestants playing for a hand built Henderson guitar and a lineup of Appalachian musicians who come because they know him.
buzz: The competition draws serious pickers and the crowd sits on the grass in the shade. People call it the friendliest festival in the state and the raffle guitar is the reason many buy tickets.

name: Damascus Trail Days
customer: Thru hikers, section hikers, gear nerds
unique: The largest Appalachian Trail festival in the country, held in a town the trail runs straight through, with a hiker parade, gear vendors, free food lines and thousands of thru hikers walking in from the woods.
buzz: Hikers plan their whole year around it and locals open their yards. The parade of hikers through town is the photograph, and the gear repairs are free.

name: Guest River Gorge Trail
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A rail trail on the old Norfolk and Western grade along the Guest River, running through three tunnels and over trestles above a gorge with sandstone cliffs, roughly five and a half miles one way and almost flat the whole way.
buzz: The tunnels and the river access are what people come for, and the flat grade makes it the walk locals recommend to anyone who does not want a climb. Watch for falling rock signs.

name: Hillsville Labor Day Flea Market and Gun Show
dates: Labor Day weekend, Friday–Monday, plus Memorial Day
company: Hillsville Volunteer Fire Department and VFW
unique: One of the largest flea markets on the east coast, spreading over the fairground and every side street in a town of 2,700, with guns, antiques, tools, produce, fried food and livestock, run by volunteer fire and VFW groups as a fundraiser.
buzz: People come from a dozen states with trailers. Dealers say the good tools go Friday morning, and locals warn about the traffic on Route 58.

name: Sherando Lake Recreation Area
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
customer: Families, swimmers, campers from the valley
unique: A spring fed mountain lake built by the CCC at the foot of the Blue Ridge with a sandy beach, a roped swim area, a second smaller lake for fishing, and trails that climb straight up into the national forest.
buzz: The beach fills by ten on July weekends and locals go on weekdays. Campground books out early and the water stays cold even in August.

name: State Arboretum of Virginia
company: University of Virginia, Blandy Experimental Farm
unique: Seven hundred acres of University of Virginia research farmland with the largest collection of boxwood in North America, a ginkgo grove that turns gold in one week, and a two mile loop through labeled trees, free and open every day.
buzz: The ginkgo grove in November is the photograph everyone takes. Birders work the meadows in migration and the place stays quiet because almost nobody knows it exists.

name: Sunspots Studios
cost: Free to watch, classes $60 and up
dates: Year round, demos most days until mid afternoon
customer: Craft curious, families, people buying gifts
unique: A working hot shop downtown where four glassblowers rotate through live demonstrations all day, with a gallery of their work and classes that put you at the bench making a paperweight or ornament.
buzz: The demo is free and people stay for two or three rounds of it. The beginner glass class is the birthday and anniversary booking in town.

name: Woodrow Wilson Presidential Library and Museum
unique: The manse where Wilson was born in 1856, with the family's furniture in place, a museum on his presidency and the League of Nations fight, a World War One trench exhibit, and the Pierce-Arrow limousine that carried him to his inauguration.
buzz: The trench recreation and the stroke story are what visitors remember. Some find the presentation old fashioned, and the docents are the ones who bring it alive.

name: York River State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A tidewater park on the York with a beach where Miocene whale bones and shark teeth wash out of the cliff, boat rentals on Taskinas Creek, and trails through marsh and hardwood that are flat enough for small kids.
buzz: Fossil hunting is the draw and rangers will tell you what you found. The creek paddle at high tide is the other reason people come back.

name: Attucks Theatre
customer: Music fans, history people, community events
unique: A 1919 theater built and financed by Black businessowners in the Huntersville neighborhood, part of the chitlin circuit that booked Duke Ellington and Cab Calloway, restored in 2004 and still running concerts and plays under its original name.
buzz: The restoration is beautiful and the sightlines from the balcony are good. Locals talk about the history as much as the shows.

name: Big Walker Lookout
unique: A hundred foot steel observation tower on the crest of Big Walker Mountain, built by a local family in the 1940s and still run by them, with a country store below selling candy, crafts and sandwiches and a view over five states on a clear day.
buzz: The tower sways a little and the stairs are open, which is either the appeal or the problem. The store's country ham biscuits and the birding from the deck are the recurring reviews.

name: Buzzard Rock
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A four mile climb from a forest road above Front Royal to a quartzite outcrop with a straight drop and a view over the town, the Shenandoah and the Blue Ridge, close enough to Washington for a half day trip.
buzz: The last stretch is steep and rocky and people warn about it. The payoff view is one of the best in northern Virginia and the lot fills by nine on weekends.

name: Historic Crab Orchard Museum and Pioneer Park
unique: A museum of the Virginia frontier with fourteen original log and stone buildings moved to the site, including a cabin, a barn, a blacksmith shop and a one room school, plus galleries on the Cherokee presence and the first settlers in the valley.
buzz: The pioneer village is the part kids like and the collection inside is better than a county museum has any right to be. Volunteers demonstrate crafts on event days.

name: Pinnacle Natural Area Preserve
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A limestone gorge where Big Cedar Creek drops through a series of falls into the Clinch River, with a trail along the water, cliffs used by nesting ravens and a great blue heron rookery downstream.
buzz: The falls and the heron rookery are the draws, and the trail is short enough for a half day. Spring wildflowers are the local secret.

name: Rockingham County Fair
customer: Farm families, teens, demolition derby crowds
unique: Virginia's largest county fair, running six days of livestock shows, a rodeo, truck and tractor pulls and a demolition derby at a permanent fairground south of Harrisonburg, with the state's biggest 4-H presence.
buzz: Locals treat it as the end of summer. The derby and the rodeo sell out the grandstand, and the livestock barns are full of kids who have been showing since they could walk.

name: Southwest Virginia Museum
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
customer: History people, families, coal country researchers
unique: A rambling 1895 Victorian mansion built by a coal and iron speculator, now a state museum of the coalfields with rooms of mining tools, company scrip, furniture and photographs of the boom towns that grew and emptied within a lifetime.
buzz: The house itself is the surprise in a town of this size, and the mining collection is more personal than institutional. Staff are happy to talk about specific camps.

name: Virginia Highlands Festival
cost: Free to browse, some events ticketed
dates: Late July into early August, about ten days
unique: Ten days of juried craft shows, antiques, author talks, music and theatre across Abingdon, running since 1949 and using the whole town, including the Barter Theatre and the historic district, as its venue.
buzz: The antiques and craft market is the draw and people come back every year for specific dealers. Locals complain about parking and go anyway.

name: Woodstock Tower
dates: Year round, forest road may close in winter
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A forest service lookout tower at the end of a short climb above the town, looking down on the seven bends of the Shenandoah and across to the Massanutten range, built by the CCC and reachable by car with a two mile walk if the gate is open.
buzz: Locals send visitors here instead of the national park because the view of the river bends is better and there is no entrance fee. Sunset is the time.

name: Wren Building at William and Mary
dates: Weekdays and Saturdays, student tours on a schedule
customer: Architecture people, prospective students, history buffs
unique: The oldest academic building in continuous use in the United States, begun in 1695 and rebuilt twice after fires, with the original chapel, the Great Hall and a courtyard where the college's students drilled before marching off to war.
buzz: Student guides from the Spotswood Society tell the fire and rebuilding story better than any plaque. Free, and the quietest hour in a town built on tourism.

name: Clinch River State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: Virginia's first blueway state park, a string of riverfront parcels along the Clinch connected by canoe access rather than roads, with the Sugar Hill unit at St. Paul open for hiking and biking above the water.
buzz: Paddlers treat the Clinch as the best smallmouth bass river in the state and the park is built around putting in and taking out. Facilities are still being built, so expect portable toilets and rough parking.

name: Comers Rock Overlook
dates: Year round, forest road may be rough
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A stone fire tower on a 4,102 foot knob at the edge of the Mount Rogers high country, with a catwalk view over the New River valley and ridges stacked to the horizon, reached by a short walk from a forest road.
buzz: Locals send visitors here instead of the crowded park overlooks. The tower steps are steep and the road up is gravel, which keeps the crowd down.

name: Elizabeth Furnace Recreation Area
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: The stone stack of an 1836 iron furnace that ran on slave and immigrant labor and cast stoves and kettles until the 1880s, standing beside a creek swimming hole and a picnic ground in a valley reached by one road over the mountain.
buzz: The furnace stack is a five minute walk and kids end up in the creek behind it. Campers use it as a base for the Massanutten trails.

name: Green Valley Book Fair
dates: Six events a year, roughly ten days each
unique: A 30,000 square foot warehouse south of Harrisonburg stacked with hundreds of thousands of publisher overstock books at a fraction of cover price, open only a few weeks a year and drawing people from several states on opening day.
buzz: People bring boxes and a list. The schedule is posted a year ahead because regulars plan trips around it, and the children's section is where the damage gets done.

name: Kline's Dairy Bar
customer: Students, families, anyone in line after a ball game
unique: Frozen custard made fresh daily since 1943 in a walk-up window downtown, with a flavor of the week that people check online and a chalkboard that has launched arguments about black raspberry versus vanilla.
buzz: The line at night is the institution. Locals order a small and get a mountain, and the flavor of the week is a genuine topic of conversation in town.

name: Patsy Cline Historic House
unique: The duplex where Patsy Cline lived as a teenager, with the family's furniture, her record collection and a guide who tells the story of the Winchester window dresser who became the first woman inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame.
buzz: Small, personal and led by people who knew the family. Fans leave saying they learned things no documentary covered. Closed in winter.

name: Wayne Theatre
dates: Year round, season runs fall to spring
customer: Theatre goers, touring band fans, families at holiday shows
unique: A 1926 vaudeville and movie house on Main Street, restored after decades dark, with a small balcony, an art gallery in the lobby and a season of touring concerts, plays and classic films that a town of 22,000 should not be able to support.
buzz: The restoration is the story locals tell, and the acoustics in a house that size are why touring acts stop. Film nights and the holiday musical sell out.

name: Williamsburg Winery at Wessex Hundred
unique: A winery on a 300 acre farm with a stone cellar built into the hillside, growing vinifera grapes in tidewater heat and running tours that end in a tasting room looking out over the vineyard.
buzz: The reserve tasting and the cellar tour are the draw, and the restaurant is a destination on its own. Reviews note the pours are generous and the property is prettier than the wines.

name: Wolf Creek Indian Village and Museum
unique: A reconstruction of a Monacan village on the footprint of an excavated 16th century settlement, with palisade, longhouses, gardens and fire pits, interpreted by staff who explain what the archaeology actually found before the village was rebuilt.
buzz: The village is small and the guides are what make it, connecting the layout to the dig records. School groups fill it on weekdays in spring.

name: Beverley Historic District
unique: A downtown grid of brick sidewalks and 19th century storefronts with cast iron porches, a 1901 opera house and a courthouse by Thomas Jefferson's firm, dense enough to cover on foot in an afternoon and used as a film set for period pictures.
buzz: Architectural Digest put it among the best main streets in the country and locals quote that. The farmer's market and the bookshops keep it from feeling like a museum.

name: Colonial Parkway
unique: A twenty three mile divided parkway with no commercial traffic, brick bridges and stone walls that links Jamestown, Williamsburg and Yorktown along the James and York rivers, built in the 1930s to look like a colonial road.
buzz: People drive it without realizing it is a national park unit. Cyclists treat the whole length as a training route and the river overlooks are the pull-offs worth stopping at.

name: Lincoln Theatre
dates: Year round, season plus film nights
customer: Music fans, film people, families at holiday shows
unique: A 1929 movie palace with a restored neon marquee and Spanish colonial interior on Marion's main street, reopened as a performing arts center that books bluegrass, country and touring acts and still runs films.
buzz: The restoration and the acoustics get the praise, and the Crooked Road music shows are the local favorites. The marquee is the photograph of downtown.

name: Luray Zoo, a Rescue Zoo
unique: A small private zoo built entirely around surrendered and confiscated animals, with a reptile house, big cats and primates that came from the pet trade, and signs that explain why the animals are there rather than just naming them.
buzz: It is honest about being a rescue rather than a showcase, and visitors say the staff will talk for twenty minutes about an individual animal's history. Not a polished attraction, and better for it.

name: Shenandoah County Fair
customer: Local families, harness racing fans, livestock exhibitors
unique: One of the oldest county fairs in the state, with a half mile harness racing track that still runs live meets, plus the usual 4-H barns, tractor pull and a grandstand that has been rebuilt around the same oval.
buzz: The harness races are the thing outsiders do not expect. Regulars come for the track and the livestock, and the fair still feels like a county event rather than a carnival.

name: Staunton Braves at Gypsy Hill Park
customer: Families, baseball people, summer night crowds
unique: Summer collegiate baseball in a 1930s WPA stone stadium inside a 214 acre city park, where the players stay with host families and the crowd sits close enough to hear the infield talk, with a pool and a miniature train in the same park.
buzz: Cheap tickets, real baseball and a small grandstand that fills on fireworks nights. Locals bring chairs to the berm and let kids run.

name: Stonewall Jackson's Headquarters Museum
unique: The house Jackson used as his headquarters in the winter of 1861 and 1862, kept almost intact with his camp desk, the original furniture and the window where he is said to have stood watching the town, plus a collection of Confederate uniforms and documents.
buzz: The intact interior is the draw, and guides tie each room to specific months of the valley campaign. Visitors say it is the most personal of the Winchester Civil War sites.

name: The Cheese Shop
customer: Locals on lunch break, tourists, picnic packers
unique: A Merchants Square shop that has sold cheese, wine and its own house dressing since the early 1970s, with a sandwich counter in the back that working Williamsburg orders from and a bread end basket by the register.
buzz: The house dressing and the sandwich line are the whole review. Locals avoid it at noon in summer and go at two.

name: The Dayton Market
customer: Food shoppers, furniture hunters, Mennonite country visitors
unique: A big indoor market where Old Order Mennonite families sell hand built oak furniture, quilts, canned goods, fry pies and still warm apple pie from stalls they run themselves, in a barn-like building on the edge of Dayton.
buzz: The fry pies and the deli counter draw people from Harrisonburg weekly. Furniture buyers come with truck measurements and leave with a table.

name: William King Museum of Art
customer: Art people, regional history fans, families
unique: A free museum in a former school building with galleries of Appalachian decorative arts and regional painting, a studio wing for classes, and a permanent collection that treats southwest Virginia furniture and pottery as fine art.
buzz: Free admission and a serious craft collection. Visitors are surprised by the quality and by how much of it is local, and the gift shop is where people buy regional pottery.

name: Augusta County Fair
customer: Farm families, livestock exhibitors, ride crowds
unique: One of the oldest county fairs in Virginia, running since the 1860s at the Augusta Expo grounds, with beef and dairy shows, a tractor pull, harness racing history in the grandstand and a midway that still fits on one gravel lot.
buzz: The livestock barns are the real event and the exhibitors have been coming for generations. Fairgoers say it is smaller than Rockingham's and easier to walk.

name: Barns of Rose Hill
dates: Year round, most shows Friday and Saturday
customer: Folk and Americana fans, local arts crowd
unique: Two restored early 20th century dairy barns turned into a listening room and gallery, with a season of folk, bluegrass and roots acts in a space small enough that the audience sits within thirty feet of the stage.
buzz: The barn acoustics are the review, along with how cheap the tickets are for the caliber of act. Berryville turns out for it.

name: Bootlegger's Run
customer: Motorcyclists, sports car drivers, history curious
unique: A mapped driving route out of Grundy that follows the ridge roads and hollows used by moonshiners running liquor to West Virginia, with waypoints on the old still sites, river crossings and switchbacks that made the route hard to patrol.
buzz: Drivers describe it as the quiet alternative to the famous motorcycle roads, with almost no traffic and some very rough pavement. The history panels are the part people did not expect.

name: Edinburg Mill
dates: Year round, restaurant closed early in the week
unique: A four story 1848 grist mill that survived Sheridan's burning of the valley, now a museum of milling and valley farm life with the original machinery in place and a restaurant in the mill room.
buzz: The volunteers know the mill's escape from the 1864 fire in detail. Visitors come for the building and stay for the exhibits on how flour got made.

name: Jackson Ferry Shot Tower
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A seventy five foot stone tower built in 1807 to drop molten lead through a sieve into water, making round shot for the frontier, standing on a cliff above the New River with the original shaft still inside.
buzz: The process is the interesting part and the setting on the river bluff is better than the tower itself. A short stop that photographers stretch out.

name: Long Branch Historic House and Farm
dates: House Monday–Wednesday, grounds daily, summer concerts
customer: Architecture people, wedding parties, concert goers
unique: An 1811 Jeffersonian mansion with a two story portico on a working farm near Millwood, open for tours of the house and its slave quarters, and used for outdoor summer concerts on the lawn.
buzz: The house is beautifully sited and the restoration is ongoing, so tours vary. Locals know it for the summer music series more than the interiors.

name: Museum of the Middle Appalachians
unique: A museum built around the salt marsh and fossil beds at Saltville, where mammoth and mastodon bones and a 14,000 year old human footprint have come out of the same ground that later fed a Confederate salt works and a chemical plant.
buzz: The Ice Age fossils and the salt industry story in one small building is the appeal, and volunteers will explain the excavation history. It is a five dollar hour that surprises people.

name: Page Valley Fair
customer: Local families, demolition derby crowds, livestock people
unique: A county fair that still runs on 4-H livestock shows, a tractor pull and a demolition derby in front of the Blue Ridge, now in its seventies and small enough that the same families have been showing animals for three generations.
buzz: The derby fills the grandstand and the fair food is the fair food. Locals say it is the week the county actually turns out.

name: Rex Theater
unique: A 1940 movie house on Galax's main street with an art deco marquee, restored as a live music room that books bluegrass, country and gospel and hosts the Friday night bluegrass series that locals treat as a standing appointment.
buzz: The sound in a small old theater is the review, and tickets are cheap. It is the year round answer to the festival crowd.

name: Virginia Zoo
customer: Families with young kids, animal people
unique: A zoo that has been operating since 1900 on land beside the Lafayette River, with an African trail, a tiger exhibit and a farmyard, small enough to finish in an afternoon and old enough to have generations of Norfolk families in its membership rolls.
buzz: Parents call it the right size for small kids and praise the train and the splash area. It is not a destination zoo, and nobody claims otherwise.

name: White Oak Lavender Farm
dates: May–August peak bloom, grounds open spring–fall
unique: Eight thousand lavender plants on a working farm with a distillation shed, a u-pick field in June and July, and a tasting room for lavender lemonade and wine from the vineyard next door, run by a family that started with a hobby row.
buzz: The bloom window is short and people plan around it. The distillation demo and the animals in the barn keep kids occupied while adults sit on the porch.

name: Wright's Dairy Rite
customer: Local families, car clubs, milkshake people
unique: A drive-in with carhop service on a curved canopy, serving burgers and milkshakes to cars parked in the same spots since the 1950s, with the original neon sign still standing over Greenville Avenue.
buzz: The carhops still come to the window and the milkshakes are the order. It is the stop people show visitors when they want to prove Staunton is not all Shakespeare.

name: Dismal Creek Wilderness
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A roadless pocket of the Jefferson National Forest where Dismal Creek runs clear over sandstone, with the Appalachian Trail following it for miles, brook trout in the pools and a waterfall a short walk from a forest road.
buzz: Quiet even in summer, and the creek is the reason. Anglers keep it to themselves and hikers use it as a gentle AT section.

name: Explore More Discovery Museum
unique: A hands-on children's museum downtown with a full sized ambulance, a bank vault, a television studio and a maker space, built into two floors of a former department store.
buzz: Parents say it buys three hours on a rainy day and the staff keep the exhibits working, which is not universal in children's museums.

name: Front Royal Festival of Leaves
customer: Leaf peepers, local families, craft fair shoppers
unique: A one day street festival in a town that sits at the north gate of Skyline Drive, with craft vendors, bluegrass and old time bands on the gazebo, a car show and food from church kitchens, timed to the color change.
buzz: Small, free and genuinely local. Visitors pair it with a drive on Skyline and say the town is at its best that weekend.

name: Jamestown-Scotland Ferry
unique: A free state run car ferry that crosses the James River on a twenty minute ride between Jamestown and Surry, running around the clock since the 1920s and carrying anyone who shows up, no ticket and no reservation.
buzz: Locals use it as a shortcut and visitors use it as a boat ride that costs nothing. Dolphins and bald eagles are a common sight from the deck.

name: Luray Carillon Singing Tower
dates: Recitals spring through fall, tower grounds year round
company: Town of Luray and Luray Caverns
customer: Music people, couples, anyone parked in town
unique: A 117 foot stone tower holding a 47 bell carillon, donated by the Luray Caverns family and played in free outdoor recitals that you listen to from the lawn, one of the few carillons in the country a passerby can walk up to.
buzz: People stumble onto a recital without knowing the tower existed and stay for the whole thing. The bells carry across the whole town.

name: Muscarelle Museum of Art
customer: Art students, drawing crowds, rainy day visitors
unique: A university museum with a small permanent collection and a habit of landing old master drawings and prints that belong in a much bigger city, mounted in a building on the William and Mary campus.
buzz: Exhibitions rotate often and the shows are ambitious for the space. Free admission makes it an easy hour between historic area tickets.

name: Old Town Winchester Walking Mall
unique: Four blocks of brick pedestrian street with 18th and 19th century buildings, a Civil War era courthouse, independent restaurants and a Saturday farmer's market, in a town that changed hands dozens of times during the war.
buzz: Lively on weekend evenings and quiet on weekday mornings. Locals point visitors to the restaurants on the mall rather than the chains out on the highway.

name: Route 11 Potato Chips
dates: Monday–Saturday, weekday mornings best for frying
unique: A kettle chip plant with a viewing gallery where you watch a batch go from sliced potatoes to bagged chips, and a counter selling warm chips and flavors that never make it to grocery shelves.
buzz: Everyone says to go on a weekday morning when the fryer is running. The salt and vinegar and the Mama Zuma's Revenge are the ones people carry out by the case.

name: Route 11 Yard Crawl
dates: Second Saturday in August, one day
unique: Forty three miles of yard sales and shop clearances along the old valley turnpike from Stephens City to New Market, with the highway reduced to a slow rolling crawl and everything from tractor parts to furniture on the shoulder.
buzz: People start at dawn with a truck and a cooler. Dealers from several states work it, and locals say the good pieces are gone by eight.

name: Virginia Quilt Museum
unique: Three floors of rotating exhibitions in an 1850s mill building, covering everything from 19th century album quilts to contemporary art quilts, with the state's best collection of documented Virginia-made bedcovers.
buzz: Quilters come from out of state for the exhibitions and the staff will explain the pattern and the dating. Non-quilters are surprised by how much of it reads as painting.

name: Williamsburg Farmers Market
unique: A Saturday market in Merchants Square with produce, oysters, cheese, baked goods and plants from farms within a couple of hours, set among restored 18th century buildings and busy enough that the whole square smells like coffee and bread.
buzz: Small but well curated, and locals treat it as the real town underneath the historic area. The oyster and baked goods stands sell out early.

name: Augusta Stone Church
dates: Grounds year round, church open for services and by arrangement
unique: A stone meeting house built in 1749 and still in use, the oldest church west of the Blue Ridge in continuous service, with the original walls, galleries and graveyard full of German and Scotch-Irish settlers who came down the valley road.
buzz: Visitors come for the graveyard and the hand cut stone. Services still happen here, which is the part people find hard to believe.

name: Bridgewater Lawn Party
customer: Local families, engine collectors, carnival crowds
unique: A fire company fundraiser that turned into four days of steam and gas engines, antique tractors, a carnival midway and food stands on the Oakdale grounds, running since the 1930s and still staffed by volunteers.
buzz: The engine show is the part outsiders do not know about. Locals go every night of it, and the fire company still keeps the money.

name: Camera Heritage Museum
unique: Over two thousand cameras packed into a downtown storefront, from wooden plate cameras and spy cameras to the first Leicas and Polaroids, collected by a camera repairman who will take one apart in front of you.
buzz: Visitors call it a hoard in the best sense and say the owner talks them through the mechanics of anything they point at. It closed for a while and is open again.

name: Dinosaur Land
unique: Fifty fiberglass dinosaurs, a giant octopus and a shark in the mouth of a concrete sea monster, built by hand starting in 1963 and never updated, on a highway named for Stonewall Jackson.
buzz: Gloriously unreconstructed and cheap. Adults who came as kids bring their own children, and photographers treat it as a shrine to mid century roadside America.

name: Hillsville Courthouse and the 1911 Shootout
customer: Local history people, true crime readers
unique: The courthouse where five people were killed in 1911 when the Allen family opened fire during a land dispute trial, a shootout that produced one of the largest manhunts in Virginia history and a folk ballad still sung in the county.
buzz: Locals tell the story better than any sign, and the bullet damage and the jail are the details people ask about. The annual play about the shootout draws a crowd.

name: Marker-Miller Orchards
cost: Free to enter, $2–$4 per pound picked
dates: August–November for apples, market year round
unique: A century farm east of Winchester with pick your own apples, peaches and pumpkins, a bakery turning out apple cider doughnuts, and a farm market that sells the fruit that did not make the grade.
buzz: The doughnuts are the reason people go and the u-pick is why they stay. Fall weekends are crowded enough to warrant going early.

name: Yorktown Market Days
dates: Saturday mornings, April–December, plus themed markets
unique: A Saturday market on the Riverwalk Landing beach at the bottom of the Yorktown bluff, with produce, seafood, baked goods and food trucks, and a view of the York River that makes people stay longer than they planned.
buzz: The setting is the review. Themed markets through the year, including a maritime festival and a harvest market, draw bigger crowds than the regular Saturdays.

name: Clarke County Fair
customer: Farm families, local teens, carnival crowds
unique: A fair run entirely by the local Ruritan Club since the 1950s, with a carnival midway, tractor pull, horse pull, livestock shows and a demolition derby on a fairground that is a hayfield eleven months of the year.
buzz: Everyone in the county goes at least once. The horse pull and the derby are the nights that fill the stands, and the food is church stand cooking.

name: Edith J. Carrier Arboretum
customer: Walkers, birders, students, parents with strollers
unique: A 125 acre woodland arboretum on the James Madison campus with labeled tree collections, a native plant trail, a pond and a boardwalk, free and open to the public every day.
buzz: Used by locals as a quiet walking loop and by birders during migration. The azalea and rhododendron bloom in spring is the busiest week.

name: Handley Library
dates: Open library hours, tours on selected Saturdays
unique: A 1913 Beaux-Arts library with a domed rotunda, a children's room in the Romanesque basement and a genealogical collection, still operating as a public library in a building that looks like a bank vault for books.
buzz: People walk in expecting a museum and find a working library. The dome and the curved stair are the photographs, and the local history room is a serious resource.

name: Holy Cross Abbey
dates: Grounds daily, gift shop limited hours
company: Order of Cistercians of the Strict Observance
unique: A Trappist monastery in the Shenandoah with a guest house, a farm, a cemetery of plain wooden crosses and a gift shop selling bread, fruitcake and honey made by the monks, where visitors are welcome to walk and sit without a program.
buzz: People come for the silence and leave with a fruitcake. The shop's Christmas orders are a local tradition that outruns the monks' ability to bake.

name: John W. Flannagan Dam and Reservoir
unique: A Corps of Engineers flood control lake of eleven hundred acres in a mountain hollow, with a campground, a beach, a marina and bass fishing that local anglers rate among the best in the coalfields.
buzz: Quiet and cheap compared with the state parks, and the campground fills on summer weekends. The dam and spillway are worth the walk.

name: Kernstown Battlefield
customer: Civil War students, walkers, dog owners
unique: The ground of two battles fought over the same ridge a year apart, in 1862 and 1864, preserved by a volunteer association with a visitor center in a farmhouse, earthworks, and a walking loop over the slope where the fighting turned.
buzz: Volunteers run it and will walk the line with you. Quiet, free, and less visited than the Winchester battlefield sites, which locals count as a virtue.

name: Watermen's Museum
customer: Boat people, families, Chesapeake history fans
unique: A small museum on the Yorktown waterfront about the people who made a living from the bay: skipjack models, crab pots, oyster tongs, decoys and tools, with working watermen often on hand to explain what each one did.
buzz: Volunteers who actually worked the water are the reason to go, and the view from the back deck over the York is free with admission. Fifteen minutes if you skim, an hour if you talk.

name: Bristol Sign on State Street
customer: Roadside collectors, photographers, everyone passing through
unique: The neon sign over State Street that reads Bristol, A Good Place to Live and straddles the state line, so you can stand with one foot in Virginia and one in Tennessee under a landmark that has been photographed since the 1910s.
buzz: It is a two minute stop that everyone photographs, and the state line painted down the middle of the street is the other half of the ritual. Downtown has been rebuilt around it with breweries and shops.

name: Hupp's Hill Civil War Park
customer: Civil War students, families, I-81 travelers
unique: A wooded hill above Strasburg where Confederate earthworks are still cut into the ground and a small museum holds artifacts dug from the battlefield, on the site of a signal station used in the 1864 valley campaign.
buzz: A quiet free stop with original trenches you can walk through. The museum is small and the volunteers are the ones who make it worth the detour.

name: The Art Space on 211
dates: Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday afternoons, or by chance
customer: Art browsers, people escaping a rainy cavern day
unique: A rambling gallery in a converted building on Route 211 showing dozens of valley artists and craftspeople at once, from plein air painters to potters to furniture makers, with the artists often sitting the desk.
buzz: Long time Luray stop that changed its name from the Warehouse Art Gallery and moved up the highway. Visitors describe it as bigger inside than it looks and full of things priced for actual houses.

name: Abram's Delight
unique: Winchester's oldest house, a 1754 stone and log home built by a Quaker family that held the first meetings in the area, with the original cooking hearth and a collection of valley furniture.
buzz: A quiet twenty minute tour with volunteers who know the family tree. The spring house and garden are the part people linger in.

name: Cooter's Place in Luray
dates: Year round, closed some weekdays in winter
customer: Dukes of Hazzard fans, roadside collectors, kids
unique: Ben Jones, the actor who played Cooter, keeps a free museum of the television show here: the General Lee, the tow truck, costumes and a replica garage, moved over the mountain from Sperryville to a bigger building on Route 211.
buzz: Free admission and unapologetically devoted to one 1980s show. Fans spend an hour, everyone else takes fifteen minutes and photographs the car.

name: Honaker Redbud Festival
customer: Local families, craft vendors, car show crowds
unique: A spring festival timed to the redbud bloom on the hills around a small Russell County town, with a parade, crafts, a car show and music, and hillsides that turn pink for about ten days a year.
buzz: Locals say the bloom is the real attraction and the festival is the excuse. It is small, free and entirely local.

name: Rocktown History
customer: Genealogists, local history people, rainy day families
unique: The county historical society's museum and research library in Dayton, with Civil War collections, valley furniture, a genealogy room that draws people from other states, and exhibits on the Mennonite and German settlement of the Shenandoah.
buzz: The genealogy volunteers are the reason people drive in. The museum side is compact and the bookstore is well stocked on local titles.

name: Waynesboro Street Arts Trail
unique: A self guided walk past a dozen large murals and painted utility boxes through downtown and along the South River, with a map that ties each piece to the artist and the building it is on.
buzz: A free hour that has turned a quiet Main Street into something people photograph. The river greenway section is the pleasant surprise.

name: Meems Bottom Covered Bridge
unique: A 204 foot single span over the North Fork, the longest remaining covered bridge in Virginia, burned by arson in 1976 and rebuilt by the county, still carrying a rural road across the river.
buzz: A five minute stop that photographers stretch to half an hour. The truss structure inside is visible from the roadway and the river shallows below are a wading spot in summer.

name: Shenandoah Valley Art Center
customer: Art browsers, gift shoppers, local artists
unique: A nonprofit community art center in a Main Street building with changing exhibitions by valley artists, working studios, and classes in clay, painting and printmaking open to anyone who signs up.
buzz: Small, free and genuinely local, with shows that rotate often enough that regulars stop in monthly. The gift shop is where people buy valley made pottery.

name: The Russell Museum
customer: Outsider art fans, seekers, the incurably curious
unique: The painted canvases and sculpted figures of Walter Russell, a early 20th century sculptor and self taught cosmologist who wrote about light and consciousness, kept in a small museum run by the philosophical university he founded in this valley town.
buzz: A strange and sincere place that most visitors had never heard of. People either find it profound or walk through in fifteen minutes, and both reviews exist.
